newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan cult guru ejected from court again.
newsitem.headline: Japan cult guru ejected from court again.

text.p: The head of a doomsday cult on trial for a deadly Tokyo subway gas attack was literally picked up and hauled away from a courtroom on Friday after repeatedly interrupting proceedings.

Shoko Asahara, leader of the Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect), interrupted the cross-examination of a former disciple by his lawyers by standing several times and demanding to be given a chance to speak.
"I want to make my position clear," Asahara told presiding judge Fumihiro Abe.
But the chief judge refused and said: "You must not interrupt the cross-examination."
The unkempt and bearded cult leader ranted throughout the proceedings, saying he himself was a victim of society.
"This court is crazy...but you can go ahead with it. Since I've been born you've been doing as you like to me."
He added: "There was no sarin from the beginning... There is no point in having this ridiculous trial."
"You can take me to the place of execution if you like... I don't know how much longer I can go on like this," screamed Asahara as he was carted away by nine security officers.

Asahara, whose real name is Chizuo Matsumoto, faces death by hanging if found guilty of murder and other charges for the March 21, 1995, sarin nerve gas attack on Tokyo's subway system which killed 12 people and made 6,000 ill.
He has yet to enter a plea.
In the absence of the cult leader, his defence continued Friday's cross-examination of Yoshihiro Inoue, 26, a former chief of the sect's "Intelligence Unit".

Inoue told the court of how cult members planned the gas attack meticulously, measuring air currents in the Tokyo subway system to determine where the most efficient area would be to place the 11 bags of deadly sarin nerve gas.

It was the second time the 41-year-old Asahara has been ejected from Tokyo District Court, following his expulsion from the courtroom on November 7 when he turned the proceedings into a near-farce with repeated interruptions and incoherent remarks.
Apart from the subway attack, Asahara is on trial for a host of other crimes, including another gas attack, kidnapping and murder.
More that 100 other members of the cult are also on trial in connection with its activities.
